title: Logical and Mathematical Analytical Ability
shortDescription: Puzzle-style reasoning: handshakes, pigeonhole, weighing problems, truth-tellers and counting logic.
genZNote: The 'think, don't compute' chapter — counting tricks and logic gates that turn long problems into one line.

sections.heading: Counting Tricks
bullets: Handshakes among n people: n(n − 1)/2 (10 people → 45).
Matches in a knock-out tournament with n teams: n − 1; league (everyone plays everyone): n(n − 1)/2.
Pigeonhole principle: if n + 1 items go in n boxes, some box has two (13 people → two share a birth month).
Number of diagonals of an n-gon: n(n − 3)/2.

sections.heading: Logic Puzzles
bullets: Truth-teller (always true) and liar (always false): test each assumption for consistency.
Weighing problems: 9 identical-looking coins with one heavier → 2 weighings on a balance; 12 coins (heavier or lighter unknown) → 3 weighings.
Number properties: divisibility rules, parity, remainders.
Scheduling/ordering puzzles: build a table; eliminate impossible options.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body: Convert text into tables or equations, apply parity/divisibility/remainder reasoning, use extreme-case or small-case testing to guess a pattern, then verify.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Analytical-ability questions combine counting principles, logic puzzles and number reasoning rather than heavy calculation.

highYieldFacts: Test small cases to find patterns.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
